data.name: Karim
data.gender_notes: Karim is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Karim is an Arabic name that signifies nobility, generosity, and kindness. It is often associated with the attributes of a benevolent and charitable person. The name Karim carries the meaning “Noble, Generous, Kind” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Karim usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, generous, kind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: One of the names of Allah in Islam is 'Al-Karim', meaning The Generous or The Noble. The name Karim reflects the Islamic value of generosity and benevolence.
data.etymology: Karim belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble, Generous, Kind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karim total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Karim holds significant cultural importance, particularly within Islamic communities. It is often given as a name to newborns as a reminder to live a life of generosity, kindness, and dignity, respecting the worth of every human being. The name reflects the rich Islamic tradition of bestowing kindness, respect, and hospitality to all, as taught in the Quran and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
data.spiritual_significance: In Muslim philosophy, the spiritual significance of the name Karim can be seen as a reminder of the innate human need to cultivate virtues that contribute to personal growth and spiritual development. The name Karim represents the essence of being a moral and virtuous person reflecting the divine attributes of Allah SWT. It is believed that the act of giving and being kind not only benefits the receiver but also the giver, as it fosters deep inner peace, contentment, and proximity to Allah. Thus, Karim can be seen as a noble reminder of the importance of practicing and upholding the values of human kindness, generosity, and compassion throughout one's life.
